_meta.scope_note: Only the controls JSO directly contributes evidence to. Customers are responsible for the broader QSA-led assessment.

controls.title: Payment page scripts that are loaded and executed in the consumer's browser are managed.

subRequirements.title: A method is implemented to confirm that each script is authorized.
subRequirements.description: JSO HMAC-SHA256 watermarks (--watermark <tag> --watermark-key <key>) inject a signed header into every protected file. Verification re-derives the HMAC in constant time. A file with a valid signature under your secret key is, by definition, an authorized script.

subRequirements.title: A method is implemented to assure the integrity of each script.
subRequirements.description: JSO Ed25519-signed release attestation (--sign-release <priv.pem>) commits to per-file sha256 in a canonical-JSON-signed envelope. Stage-2 verification re-hashes the on-disk files. Any post-signing byte change breaks the signature.

subRequirements.title: An inventory of all scripts is maintained with written business or technical justification.
subRequirements.description: The manifest.json's files[] array is the technical inventory for protected first-party files. Add --script-inventory with a payment-page script CSV or JSON export when reviewers need authorization and written business justification for every script loaded on the page.

controls.title: A change- and tamper-detection mechanism is deployed for payment pages.

subRequirements.title: Detects unauthorized modification (including IoCs, changes, additions, and deletions) of HTTP headers and contents of payment pages as received by the consumer browser.
subRequirements.description: JSO Runtime Defense modules ship an integrity heartbeat, devtools/debug protection, headless detection, and tamper-aware self-defending IIFE. The watermark also remains in the protected script, so an in-browser verifier can confirm the served bytes match the signed build.

subRequirements.title: Performs the function at least once every seven days OR per the targeted risk analysis cadence.
subRequirements.description: Runtime Defense beacon callback fires on every tamper detection event AND on periodic heartbeat. Configure the cadence in your protection options (BeaconUrl + heartbeat interval) to satisfy the seven-day-or-faster requirement.

subRequirements.title: Alerts personnel to unauthorized modification.
subRequirements.description: Beacon callback emits structured JSON events to your BeaconUrl. JSO ships first-party SIEM adapters in jso-beacon-slack (Splunk HEC, Elasticsearch, generic HMAC-signed webhook) that forward those events to the on-call rota.

out_of_scope_customer_owns.note: TLS protection of the JSO HTTP API call is JSO's responsibility (HSTS, TLS 1.3); but TLS protection of the consumer's first-fetch of the protected script from your CDN is the customer's responsibility (Subresource Integrity, CSP).
JSO delivers the alert; the customer must define the on-call runbook (who pages, what they do).
Incident response plan is customer-owned. JSO contributes the detection signal only.
